title: GENNA - Complete Feature Engineering System
description: 62 Features Across 7 Categories for Instagram Post Analysis
notes: R = Reels, C = Carousels, I = Single Images. Prompts include {caption_text}, {whisper_transcript}, {ocr_text}, {caption_first_line} placeholders.

features.name: video_duration_sec
features.possible_values: Numeric (seconds). Range: 1–5400. Measured from first to last frame of the published Reel.
features.prompt: N/A — Extract programmatically using FFprobe: ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 <file>. Return the integer number of seconds rounded down.

features.name: carousel_slide_count
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Range: 2–20. Count of individual slides in a carousel post.
features.model_detail: Instagram API / Metadata extraction — no AI needed
features.prompt: N/A — Extract programmatically from Instagram API field "children.data.length" or equivalent metadata. Return the integer count of slides.

features.name: aspect_ratio
features.possible_values: vertical_9x16 — 9:16 portrait, standard Reels; vertical_4x5 — 4:5 portrait, feed-optimized; square_1x1 — 1:1 square format; horizontal_16x9 — 16:9 landscape; horizontal_other — any other landscape ratio; other — non-standard ratio
features.prompt: N/A — Extract width and height programmatically. Classify: if w/h ≈ 0.5625 → vertical_9x16; if w/h ≈ 0.8 → vertical_4x5; if w/h ≈ 1.0 → square_1x1; if w/h ≈ 1.778 → horizontal_16x9; if w/h > 1.0 and not 16:9 → horizontal_other; else → other. Use ±5% tolerance. Return only the category string.

features.name: cuts_per_minute
features.possible_values: Numeric (float, 1 decimal). Range: 0.0–60.0+. Number of scene transitions per minute of video. Analyze the full video.
features.model_detail: PySceneDetect (local CV) + calculation — no AI needed
features.prompt: N/A — Use PySceneDetect ContentDetector to count scene changes across the full video. Formula: (scene_count - 1) / (duration_sec / 60). Return float rounded to 1 decimal.

features.name: text_overlay_presence
features.possible_values: none — no visible text overlaid on content; lower_third — text in bottom third only; upper_third — text in top third only; center — text in center area of frame; full_screen — text covers most of the frame; multi_zone — text in 2+ distinct areas
features.prompt: Analyze this image/frame for text overlaid on the visual content (NOT captions in the post description). Where is the text overlay positioned? Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; lower_third; upper_third; center; full_screen; multi_zone. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: dominant_color_palette
features.possible_values: warm — reds, oranges, yellows dominate; cool — blues, greens, purples dominate; neutral — whites, blacks, grays, beiges dominate; pastel — soft, desaturated light tones; vibrant — highly saturated bold colors; dark_moody — low brightness, dark tones; earth_tones — browns, tans, olive greens; monochrome — single color hue with variations; mixed — no single palette dominates
features.prompt: Analyze the overall color palette of this image/frame. What is the dominant color palette? Respond with exactly one value from this list: warm; cool; neutral; pastel; vibrant; dark_moody; earth_tones; monochrome; mixed. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: lighting_type
features.possible_values: natural_daylight — sunlight or window light, daytime; golden_hour — warm sunset or sunrise tones; artificial_studio — ring light, softbox, professional studio; artificial_ambient — indoor lamps, overhead lighting; low_light — dark environment, nighttime; neon_colored — neon signs, colored LED lights; mixed — combination of multiple light sources; screen_light — lit primarily by phone or monitor glow; flash — direct camera flash visible
features.prompt: Analyze the lighting in this image/frame. What is the primary lighting type? Respond with exactly one value from this list: natural_daylight; golden_hour; artificial_studio; artificial_ambient; low_light; neon_colored; mixed; screen_light; flash. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: camera_movement_style
features.possible_values: static — camera does not move, tripod or fixed; handheld — slight natural shake, person-held; smooth_pan — horizontal glide left/right; smooth_tilt — vertical glide up/down; tracking — camera follows a moving subject; dolly_zoom — push in or pull out on subject; whip_pan — fast horizontal sweep between scenes; orbit — camera circles around subject; pov — first-person point-of-view movement; drone_aerial — overhead or aerial perspective movement; mixed — multiple movement styles used. Analyze the full video.
features.prompt: Analyze the camera movement throughout this entire video. What is the PRIMARY camera movement style used most frequently? Respond with exactly one value from this list: static; handheld; smooth_pan; smooth_tilt; tracking; dolly_zoom; whip_pan; orbit; pov; drone_aerial; mixed. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: hook_visual_technique
features.possible_values: face_close_up — person's face fills the frame; product_close_up — object or product shown in detail; text_hook — bold text dominates the opening frame; action_in_progress — movement or activity already happening; reveal_tease — partial view that builds curiosity; before_after — shows a transformation starting point; screen_recording — phone or computer screen capture; reaction_shot — person reacting to something; pattern_interrupt — unexpected or jarring visual; static_scene — still or slow opening with no strong visual hook. Analyze ONLY the first 3 seconds.
features.prompt: Analyze ONLY the first 3 seconds of this video. What visual technique is used to hook the viewer? Respond with exactly one value from this list: face_close_up; product_close_up; text_hook; action_in_progress; reveal_tease; before_after; screen_recording; reaction_shot; pattern_interrupt; static_scene. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: visual_format_type
features.possible_values: talking_head — person speaking directly to camera; b_roll_only — footage montage with no person on screen; talking_head_with_broll — person speaking intercut with footage; screen_capture — screencast or phone recording; slideshow — static images or text slides with transitions; animation_motion — animated graphics or motion design; split_screen — two or more frames visible simultaneously; green_screen — background replaced with image or video; lip_sync — person lip-syncing to audio; tutorial_hands — hands-on demonstration, how-to angle; vlog_style — casual moving-camera daily life content; interview — two or more people in conversation. Analyze the full video.
features.prompt: Analyze this entire video. What is the PRIMARY visual format? Respond with exactly one value from this list: talking_head; b_roll_only; talking_head_with_broll; screen_capture; slideshow; animation_motion; split_screen; green_screen; lip_sync; tutorial_hands; vlog_style; interview. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: transition_style
features.possible_values: none — no transitions, single continuous shot; hard_cut — abrupt cuts between scenes; match_cut — seamless spatial or movement matching; swipe — directional swipe between scenes; zoom_transition — zoom in/out to next scene; fade — fade to black/white between scenes; whip — fast pan connecting scenes; object_cover — object covers lens then reveals new scene; morph — one shape transforms into another; mixed — multiple transition types used. Analyze the full video.
features.prompt: Analyze the transitions used throughout this video. What is the PRIMARY transition style? Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; hard_cut; match_cut; swipe; zoom_transition; fade; whip; object_cover; morph; mixed. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: face_presence
features.possible_values: no_face — no human face visible; single_face — exactly one face visible; multiple_faces — two or more faces visible. For Reels: analyze the thumbnail / first frame. For Carousel: analyze the first slide. For Single Image: analyze the image.
features.model_detail: MTCNN / MediaPipe Face Detection (local CV) — no AI needed
features.prompt: N/A — Use MTCNN or MediaPipe face detection on the target frame. If 0 faces detected → no_face; if 1 → single_face; if ≥2 → multiple_faces. Return only the category string.

features.name: image_quality_score
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Range: 1–10. Composite score: 1–3 = low quality (blurry, pixelated, poor lighting); 4–6 = average quality (acceptable but not polished); 7–8 = high quality (sharp, well-lit, good composition); 9–10 = professional quality (studio-grade, cinematic). For Reels: analyze 3 sampled frames (first, mid, last). For Carousel: analyze first slide. For Single Image: analyze the image.
features.prompt: Rate the overall production quality of this image/frame on a scale from 1 to 10. Consider sharpness, resolution, lighting, color grading, and composition. 1-3 = low quality (blurry, pixelated, poor lighting); 4-6 = average quality; 7-8 = high quality (sharp, well-lit); 9-10 = professional/studio grade. Return ONLY a single integer from 1 to 10, nothing else.

features.name: zoom_effect_used
features.possible_values: none — no zoom effects; slow_zoom_in — gradual push toward subject; slow_zoom_out — gradual pull away from subject; fast_zoom_in — rapid punch-in for emphasis; fast_zoom_out — rapid pull-out for reveal; zoom_pulse — rhythmic zoom in/out synced to audio; mixed — multiple zoom types used. Analyze the full video.
features.prompt: Analyze this video for any zoom effects applied (digital or physical zoom in/out). What is the PRIMARY zoom effect used? Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; slow_zoom_in; slow_zoom_out; fast_zoom_in; fast_zoom_out; zoom_pulse; mixed. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: thumbnail_composition
features.possible_values: centered_subject — main subject in the center; rule_of_thirds — subject placed on grid intersections; symmetrical — balanced mirror-like composition; asymmetrical — intentionally unbalanced, dynamic; close_up — subject fills 70%+ of frame; wide_shot — subject is small, environment dominates; flat_lay — overhead shot of objects on surface; text_dominant — text is the main visual element; collage — multiple images or elements arranged together; minimal — very few elements, lots of negative space
features.prompt: Analyze the composition of this image (or first frame/thumbnail). What is the primary composition style? Respond with exactly one value from this list: centered_subject; rule_of_thirds; symmetrical; asymmetrical; close_up; wide_shot; flat_lay; text_dominant; collage; minimal. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: audio_hook_type
features.possible_values: voice_direct_address — speaker says "you" or speaks to viewer; voice_question — opens with a spoken question; voice_bold_claim — starts with a surprising statement or statistic; voice_story_opener — begins with "So…", "I just…", narrative lead-in; trending_sound — uses a recognizable trending audio clip; original_music — original or non-trending background music; sound_effect — starts with a distinct SFX (ding, whoosh, etc.); asmr_texture — tactile, whisper, or sensory-focused audio; silence — no audio or intentional silence in first 3 seconds; mixed — combination of two or more types above. Analyze ONLY the first 3 seconds of audio.
features.prompt: Listen to ONLY the first 3 seconds of this video's audio. What type of audio hook is used? Respond with exactly one value from this list: voice_direct_address; voice_question; voice_bold_claim; voice_story_opener; trending_sound; original_music; sound_effect; asmr_texture; silence; mixed. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: text_hook_on_screen
features.possible_values: question — text asks a question to the viewer; bold_claim — strong statement or surprising stat; how_to — "How to…", instructional opener; listicle — "5 things…", "3 reasons…", numbered; curiosity_gap — incomplete info that demands click/swipe ("You won't believe…"); direct_command — "Stop scrolling", "Watch this", imperative verb; quote_or_testimonial — attributed quote or social proof; label_or_title — simple descriptive title, no hook intent; none — no text visible on screen. For Reels: analyze ONLY the first frame. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze the visible text overlaid on this image/frame (ignore captions below the post). Classify the text hook type. Respond with exactly one value from this list: question; bold_claim; how_to; listicle; curiosity_gap; direct_command; quote_or_testimonial; label_or_title; none. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: curiosity_gap_level
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Range: 0–5. 0 = no curiosity gap at all, everything is revealed upfront; 1 = very mild, slight intrigue; 2 = moderate, viewer may want to know more; 3 = strong, clear information withheld to drive engagement; 4 = very strong, bold open loop that demands resolution; 5 = extreme, shocking or provocative tease with maximum withholding. For Reels: analyze first 3 seconds (video + text + audio). For Carousel: first slide (visual + text). For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze the opening of this content (first frame/slide and any visible text or audio context). Rate the curiosity gap on a scale from 0 to 5. 0 = no curiosity gap, everything revealed; 1 = very mild; 2 = moderate; 3 = strong, clear info withheld; 4 = very strong open loop; 5 = extreme, shocking tease. Return ONLY a single integer from 0 to 5, nothing else.

features.name: pattern_interrupt_type
features.possible_values: none — content blends with typical feed, no interrupt; visual_shock — unexpected image, jarring color, or extreme close-up; motion_burst — sudden fast movement or camera jerk; text_shock — provocative or contrarian text ("This is wrong", "Delete this app"); audio_spike — sudden loud sound, bass drop, or scream; fourth_wall_break — directly acknowledges the viewer scrolling ("Wait, stop"); format_break — looks like a meme, glitch, UI screenshot, or notification. For Reels: analyze first 3 seconds. For Carousel/Image: analyze first slide/image.
features.prompt: Analyze the opening of this content (first 3 seconds for video, or the first image/slide). Is there a pattern interrupt — something designed to break the viewer's scroll momentum? Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; visual_shock; motion_burst; text_shock; audio_spike; fourth_wall_break; format_break. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: opening_emotion_conveyed
features.possible_values: excitement — high energy, enthusiasm, hype; humor — funny, comedic, lighthearted; curiosity — mysterious, intriguing, makes you lean in; shock — disbelief, outrage, jaw-drop; empathy — relatable pain, struggle, vulnerability; aspiration — inspirational, motivational, "goals"; fear_urgency — FOMO, warning, scarcity, time pressure; calm_trust — soothing, authoritative, educational tone; controversy — polarizing, debate-sparking, hot take; neutral — no clear emotion, flat or informational. For Reels: analyze first 3 seconds (visual + audio + text). For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze the emotional tone conveyed in the opening of this content (first 3 seconds for video, or first slide/image). What is the PRIMARY emotion the viewer is meant to feel? Respond with exactly one value from this list: excitement; humor; curiosity; shock; empathy; aspiration; fear_urgency; calm_trust; controversy; neutral. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: first_frame_scroll_stop_score
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Range: 1–10. Composite score rating how likely this first frame is to stop a user from scrolling. 1–3 = weak (generic, low contrast, no focal point); 4–6 = moderate (decent composition but nothing remarkable); 7–8 = strong (clear focal point, bold text or face, high contrast); 9–10 = exceptional (impossible to ignore, combines multiple scroll-stopping elements). Consider: visual contrast, text readability, face presence, emotional expression, color pop, composition clarity.
features.prompt: You are an expert in Instagram content performance. Rate this image/first frame on its ability to stop a user from scrolling in their feed. Score from 1 to 10. Consider: visual contrast, bold text, face presence, emotional expression, color pop, and composition clarity. 1-3 = weak (generic, low contrast); 4-6 = moderate; 7-8 = strong (clear focal point, bold elements); 9-10 = exceptional (impossible to ignore). Return ONLY a single integer from 1 to 10, nothing else.

features.name: hook_delivery_speed
features.possible_values: instant — hook lands in first 1 second (text slap, face, loud audio); fast — hook lands between 1–2 seconds; moderate — hook lands between 2–3 seconds; slow_build — no clear hook in first 3 seconds, gradual ramp. Analyze ONLY the first 3 seconds.
features.prompt: Watch ONLY the first 3 seconds of this video. How quickly does the main hook (the element designed to capture attention) land? Respond with exactly one value from this list: instant; fast; moderate; slow_build. instant = within first 1 second; fast = 1-2 seconds; moderate = 2-3 seconds; slow_build = no clear hook in first 3 seconds. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: direct_viewer_address
features.possible_values: Boolean. yes — content directly addresses the viewer using "you", eye contact to camera, pointing, or second-person language in on-screen text; no — no direct address to the viewer. For Reels: analyze first 3 seconds (text + audio + visual). For Carousel: first slide text + visual. For Single Image: text + visual.
features.prompt: Analyze this content (first 3 seconds for video, or the image/slide). Does the creator directly address the viewer? This includes: saying "you" in audio or text, making eye contact with the camera, pointing at the camera, or using second-person language in on-screen text. Respond with exactly one value: yes; no. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: bait_and_reveal_structure
features.possible_values: none — no bait/reveal structure present; before_after — shows "before" state, promises or delivers "after"; question_then_answer — poses question up front, answer comes later; problem_then_solution — presents a pain point, then solves it; tease_then_payoff — shows a teaser/preview, full reveal follows; ranking_or_countdown — builds toward a #1 or final reveal; mystery_box — hides something, builds suspense for the uncover. For Reels: analyze the full video structure. For Carousel: analyze all slides' flow.
features.prompt: Analyze the FULL structure of this content (all slides for carousel, or entire video for Reels). Does it use a bait-and-reveal structure where something is teased or withheld early and then revealed later? Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; before_after; question_then_answer; problem_then_solution; tease_then_payoff; ranking_or_countdown; mystery_box. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: opening_subject_framing
features.possible_values: face_extreme_closeup — face fills 80%+ of frame, intense eye contact; face_medium — face visible from chest up, conversational; hands_or_object — hands doing something or object in focus, no face; full_body — person's full body visible; environment_wide — wide shot, person is small or absent; text_only_frame — frame is entirely or mostly text, no person or object; screen_or_ui — phone screen, app UI, or computer display; product_hero — product or item centered as the star of the frame; abstract_graphic — pattern, gradient, illustration, or motion graphic. For Reels: analyze ONLY the first frame. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze this image/first frame. What is the PRIMARY subject framing in the opening? Respond with exactly one value from this list: face_extreme_closeup; face_medium; hands_or_object; full_body; environment_wide; text_only_frame; screen_or_ui; product_hero; abstract_graphic. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: people_count
features.possible_values: none — no person visible in frame; one — exactly one person visible; two — exactly two people visible; small_group — 3 to 5 people visible; crowd — 6 or more people visible. For Reels: analyze a representative frame from the first 3 seconds. For Carousel: analyze the first slide. For Single Image: analyze the image. Count only clearly visible people (partial limbs or silhouettes do not count).
features.prompt: Count the number of clearly visible people in this image/frame (do not count partial limbs, silhouettes, or people in distant backgrounds who are unrecognizable). Respond with exactly one value from this list: none; one; two; small_group; crowd. none = 0 people; one = 1; two = 2; small_group = 3-5; crowd = 6+. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: primary_person_age_range
features.possible_values: child — appears under 13 years old; teen — appears 13–17 years old; young_adult — appears 18–29 years old; adult — appears 30–45 years old; middle_aged — appears 46–60 years old; senior — appears over 60 years old; mixed_ages — multiple people with clearly different age groups; not_applicable — no person visible or age not determinable. For Reels: analyze the first 3 seconds. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image. If multiple people, classify the PRIMARY person (most prominent / centered).
features.prompt: Analyze the most prominent person visible in this image/frame. What is their apparent age range based solely on visual appearance? If multiple people are visible, classify the most prominent one. Respond with exactly one value from this list: child; teen; young_adult; adult; middle_aged; senior; mixed_ages; not_applicable. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: eye_contact_with_camera
features.possible_values: Boolean. yes — the primary person is looking directly into the camera lens, creating a sense of direct viewer connection; no — no person is looking at the camera (looking away, eyes closed, no face visible, or no person present). For Reels: analyze ONLY the first frame. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze this image/frame. Is the most prominent person looking directly into the camera lens (making eye contact with the viewer)? Respond with exactly one value: yes; no. If no person is visible, respond no. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: dominant_facial_expression
features.possible_values: happy_smiling — genuine smile, joy, laughter; surprised_shocked — wide eyes, open mouth, disbelief; serious_neutral — calm, composed, no strong emotion; angry_frustrated — frown, clenched jaw, displeasure; sad_emotional — tearful, downcast, vulnerability; confident_smirk — self-assured, knowing look, slight smile; exaggerated_expressive — over-the-top reaction face, theatrical; focused_concentrated — intense focus, looking at task; not_applicable — no face visible, face obscured, or no person. For Reels: analyze ONLY the first frame. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image. Classify the PRIMARY person's expression.
features.prompt: Analyze the facial expression of the most prominent person in this image/frame. What is their dominant expression? Respond with exactly one value from this list: happy_smiling; surprised_shocked; serious_neutral; angry_frustrated; sad_emotional; confident_smirk; exaggerated_expressive; focused_concentrated; not_applicable. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: body_language_energy
features.possible_values: high_energy — animated gestures, jumping, dancing, fast movement; moderate_energy — casual movement, hand gestures while talking, walking; low_energy — still, seated, minimal movement, relaxed posture; posed_static — deliberate fashion or portrait pose, no natural movement; not_applicable — no person visible or body not shown. For Reels: analyze the first 3 seconds of video (motion matters). For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image.
features.prompt: Analyze the body language and energy level of the most prominent person in this content (first 3 seconds for video, or the image/slide). Respond with exactly one value from this list: high_energy; moderate_energy; low_energy; posed_static; not_applicable. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: talent_role_in_content
features.possible_values: speaking_to_camera — person talks directly to viewer, educational or opinion format; narrating_offscreen — voice is heard but person is not on screen (or only briefly); performing — dancing, singing, lip-syncing, acting out a scene; demonstrating — showing how to do something, hands-on tutorial; reacting — watching or responding to something on screen; interviewing — two or more people in Q&A or conversation; lifestyle_passive — person is present but not actively performing (e.g., walking, posing, eating); no_person — no human talent in the video. Analyze the full video to determine the PRIMARY role.
features.prompt: Analyze this entire video. What is the PRIMARY role of the main person (talent) in the content? Respond with exactly one value from this list: speaking_to_camera; narrating_offscreen; performing; demonstrating; reacting; interviewing; lifestyle_passive; no_person. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: appearance_style
features.possible_values: casual_everyday — t-shirt, jeans, athleisure, relaxed daily wear; professional_business — suit, blazer, business attire, office-ready; glamorous_styled — full makeup, styled hair, fashion-forward outfit; fitness_athletic — workout clothes, sportswear, gym setting; uniform_costume — work uniform, costume, cosplay, themed outfit; minimal_undone — pajamas, no makeup emphasis, "just woke up" look; not_applicable — no person visible or appearance not determinable. For Reels: analyze first 3 seconds. For Carousel: first slide. For Single Image: the image. Classify the PRIMARY person.
features.prompt: Analyze the appearance and styling of the most prominent person in this image/frame. What best describes their appearance style? Respond with exactly one value from this list: casual_everyday; professional_business; glamorous_styled; fitness_athletic; uniform_costume; minimal_undone; not_applicable. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: creator_camera_presence_score
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Range: 1–10. Composite score rating the on-camera charisma and presence of the primary person. 1–3 = low presence (stiff, monotone, uncomfortable, avoids eye contact); 4–6 = moderate (functional delivery, neither engaging nor off-putting); 7–8 = strong (confident, expressive, holds attention naturally); 9–10 = exceptional (magnetic, commanding, professional-level screen presence). Consider: vocal energy, facial expressiveness, eye contact consistency, gesture naturalness, confidence. Analyze the full video. If no person speaks to camera, return 0.
features.prompt: Analyze this entire video. Rate the on-camera presence and charisma of the primary person on a scale from 1 to 10. Consider: vocal energy, facial expressiveness, eye contact consistency, gesture naturalness, and confidence. 1-3 = low (stiff, monotone); 4-6 = moderate; 7-8 = strong (confident, expressive); 9-10 = exceptional (magnetic, commanding). If no person speaks to camera, return 0. Return ONLY a single integer from 0 to 10, nothing else.

features.name: audio_source_type
features.possible_values: original_voice_only — creator's own voice with no background music; original_voice_with_music — creator speaks over background music; voiceover_with_music — pre-recorded narration layered over music; trending_sound — uses a sound from Instagram's audio library that other creators have also used; original_music — creator's own music or a non-trending track; licensed_music_only — commercial song, no speech; sound_effects_only — SFX-driven audio, no speech or music; text_to_speech — AI-generated voice (robotic or synthetic); silent — no audio or muted content. Analyze the full audio track.
features.prompt: Analyze the FULL audio track of this video. What is the primary audio source type? Respond with exactly one value from this list: original_voice_only; original_voice_with_music; voiceover_with_music; trending_sound; original_music; licensed_music_only; sound_effects_only; text_to_speech; silent. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: speech_language
features.possible_values: ISO 639-1 language code as the value (e.g., en, pt, es, fr, de, it, ja, ko, zh, ar, hi, etc.). none — no speech detected in the audio; mixed — two or more languages spoken in the video; unintelligible — speech is present but too unclear to determine language. Analyze the full audio. Return the language of the DOMINANT spoken portion.
features.prompt: N/A — Two-step pipeline: (1) Run Whisper large-v3 with language detection enabled: whisper.transcribe(audio, task="transcribe"). Extract the detected language code from result["language"]. (2) If no speech segments detected → "none". If Whisper detects multiple language switches → "mixed". If confidence < 0.5 → "unintelligible". Return only the ISO 639-1 code or status string.

features.name: speech_pacing_wpm
features.possible_values: Numeric (integer). Unit: words per minute (WPM). Range: 0–300+. 0 = no speech detected. Reference benchmarks: slow/deliberate = 80–120 WPM; conversational = 120–160 WPM; fast/energetic = 160–200 WPM; rapid-fire = 200+ WPM. Analyze the full audio. Count only spoken words, exclude music/SFX duration from calculation.
features.prompt: N/A — Two-step pipeline: (1) Run Whisper large-v3 to transcribe the full audio with timestamps. (2) Calculate: total_words = len(transcript.split()); speech_duration_minutes = (last_word_end_time - first_word_start_time) / 60. If speech_duration_minutes > 0: WPM = round(total_words / speech_duration_minutes). If no speech: return 0. Return only the integer WPM value.

features.name: voice_tone_energy
features.possible_values: high_energy_excited — fast, loud, enthusiastic, hype delivery; confident_authoritative — strong, steady, expert or teacher tone; calm_soothing — slow, soft, ASMR-like or relaxing; casual_conversational — natural, friend-talking-to-friend tone; dramatic_storytelling — theatrical, suspenseful, narrative voice; monotone_flat — low variation in pitch and energy; whisper_intimate — intentionally quiet, close-mic, personal; comedic_playful — joking, sarcastic, exaggerated for humor; not_applicable — no human voice present in the audio. Analyze the full audio track.
features.prompt: Analyze the human voice tone and energy in this video's audio. What is the PRIMARY voice tone? Respond with exactly one value from this list: high_energy_excited; confident_authoritative; calm_soothing; casual_conversational; dramatic_storytelling; monotone_flat; whisper_intimate; comedic_playful; not_applicable. Return ONLY the value, nothing else.

features.name: background_music_mood
features.possible_values: upbeat_happy — energetic, positive, feel-good; chill_lofi — relaxed, lo-fi beats, calm vibes; epic_cinematic — dramatic, orchestral, building tension; edgy_trap — dark beats, bass-heavy, hip-hop/trap; romantic_emotional — piano, strings, sentimental; quirky_playful — fun, cartoonish, comedic underscore; suspenseful_tense — building anxiety, horror-adjacent; trending_viral — recognizable viral sound or remix; ambient_minimal — barely noticeable background texture; none — no background music present. Analyze the full audio. If voice and music both exist, classify only the MUSIC mood.
